description:
Target file: repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts. Single edit.

Locate this line. It appears exactly once in the file and is indented with six spaces:
      if (!covered) {

Insert a new block immediately BEFORE that line. Do not modify that line, and do not modify anything above it.

The block to insert gives a changed source file a second chance to count as tested, by looking for a test that imports it rather than a test named after it. Write it as follows, using no regular expressions anywhere:

Wrap everything in an if statement whose condition is that covered is currently false, and wrap the body in a try with an empty catch so any error simply leaves covered as it was.

Inside, dynamically import readdir and readFile from node:fs/promises. Build the vessel test directory by taking the target path held in tf, splitting it on forward slashes, keeping the first two segments, rejoining them with a forward slash, and appending a forward slash then the word test, all prefixed by the existing rootT value and a forward slash.

Derive the module base name by splitting tf on forward slashes, taking the last segment, and removing a trailing .ts or .tsx suffix using endsWith and slice rather than a regular expression.

Call readdir on that test directory passing an options object with recursive set to true. Iterate the returned entries. Convert each entry to a string. Skip any whose name does not end in .test.ts. Count the ones you do not skip and stop the loop once that count exceeds two hundred.

For each remaining entry, read the file as utf8 and test whether its contents include any of four needles, each built by string concatenation: a forward slash then the base name then a double quote; a forward slash then the base name then .js then a double quote; and the same two again with a single quote instead of a double quote. If any needle is present, set covered to true and break out of the loop.

The four needles must end at a quote or at .js deliberately. That is what makes this a whole-segment match instead of a prefix match. A module named gap must be matched by a specifier ending /gap or /gap.js and must NOT be matched by one ending /gap-lifecycle-scan. A prefix match would credit a module with coverage from a test that never loads it, and this count is consumed by the recovery ladder rung asserting that landed changes are known to do something, so over-reporting would make that rung state a falsehood. Under-reporting is the safe direction.

Rationale for the change: the most frequently rewritten file in this vessel is currently reported as having no test, while three test files exist whose names begin with its base name, and exactly one of them actually imports it. Matching on imports counts that one and correctly ignores the two that do not load the module.

Make no other change to this file, and change no other file.
